rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and avoid truncation. This should show whether any compounds are unretained early or still retained into the high-organic hold, guiding later narrowing of the phi window and adjustment of slope.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to cut time. The observed elution window corresponds roughly to phi_e about 0.18 to 0.68, so a narrower, steeper gradient centered on that window plus a modest temperature increase should pull the last peak earlier while likely preserving resolution.

We are very close to the ideal score, so push for a slightly faster run by shortening the gradient one step and raising temperature one step. The current worst pair still has comfortable margin (R 2.72), so this should test whether t_last can be brought to 10 min or below without losing full resolution.

You already have the maximum CRF, so this run probes how much more speed is possible before the weakest pair drops below full-credit resolution. Shortening the gradient and raising temperature one more step is the most direct way to find the boundary, with the current worst pair still having some margin.

The loss at 6 min/60 C is from the first pair, so keep the fast conditions but lower phi0 one step to retain and spread the earliest peaks more while leaving the late part largely unchanged. This directly tests whether the critical pair can be restored to full resolution without sacrificing the short run.

Lowering phi0 improved the first pair from 1.29 to 1.47 while keeping the run very short, so one more step down should be enough to restore full-credit resolution. This is the most targeted way to try to match or beat the current best score with a faster method.

At 6 min and 60 C the only remaining issue is the first pair sitting right at the resolution threshold, and narrowing the gradient window from the top should slightly flatten the slope without changing the early start. This may lift the critical pair above 1.5 while keeping the run essentially as fast as the current 6 min methods.

The 6 min method at 60 C is essentially at the edge, so back off temperature one step to recover resolution margin while keeping the same very short gradient. This should improve the borderline first pair and still keep the last peak well under 10 min.

You now have a fully resolved 6 min method with margin, so test a slightly narrower upper window at the same temperature to see if selectivity remains acceptable while possibly tightening the run further. The key question is whether the late critical pair stays above 1.5 at this milder temperature.

This tests whether phi0 can be raised one step while preserving full resolution, which would make the method a bit less retentive at the front and may indicate the true edge of the robust operating window. The current 6 min, 55 C method has good margin, so mapping this boundary is the most useful next refinement.

Since phi0 0.10 still gives full resolution at 6 min and 55 C, raise phi0 one more step to find the upper edge for the earliest critical pair while likely keeping the short run. This boundary check can identify the most aggressive robust method among the 6 min conditions.

The 6 min, 55 C method still has full-credit resolution at phi0 0.15, so push phi0 one more step to see if the front can be accelerated further before the first pair fails. This is the most direct remaining way to locate the fastest fully resolved condition in the current neighborhood.

Phi0 0.15 is the fastest fully resolved front end so far; increasing phi1 one step will steepen the gradient slightly and may pull the last peak earlier while preserving enough margin on the first pair. This tests whether the 6 min, 55 C optimum can be made even faster without crossing the resolution threshold.

The move to phi1 0.70 improved speed while maintaining full resolution, so push phi1 one more step higher to see if the last peak can be shortened further without the early critical pair dropping below 1.5. This is the most promising remaining direction for a faster fully resolved 6 min method.

Resolution remains acceptable as phi1 increases and the last peak keeps moving earlier, so continue in the same direction by raising phi1 one more step. This should locate the upper phi1 boundary where the first pair finally loses full-credit resolution.

The first pair is now just above the 1.5 threshold at phi1 0.80, making phi1 0.85 the logical next step to find the true limit of the fastest fully resolved 6 min method. This should show whether there is still a little more room to shorten the chromatogram or whether 0.80 is already the optimum edge.

At phi1 0.80 the method is right at the resolution boundary, so lowering phi0 one step should selectively recover margin for the first pair while keeping the very short run and high phi1. This tests whether a slightly broader low-end window can make the 0.80 method more robust without giving up much speed.

Lowering phi0 restored margin at phi1 0.80, so the next useful boundary test is phi1 0.85 with the same lower start. This checks whether the faster late elution seen at higher phi1 can be achieved while keeping the first pair at or above full-credit resolution.

At phi0 0.10 and phi1 0.85 the first pair is still just above threshold, so one more phi1 step is the clearest way to find the absolute upper boundary of the fastest fully resolved method. If resolution fails, that confirms 0.85 as the best aggressive setting; if it holds, you gain an even shorter run.

Since phi1 0.85 is fully resolved at phi0 0.10 and phi1 0.90 fails, lowering phi0 one step at phi1 0.85 should test whether the same fast upper window can be made more robust on the critical first pair. This helps define the best practical 6 min operating point near the optimum boundary.

Phi1 0.90 failed at phi0 0.10 but only on the first pair, so lowering phi0 to 0.05 may recover enough early retention to restore full resolution while keeping the shortest late elution tested so far. This is the best remaining chance to find an even faster fully resolved method than the current phi1 0.85 runs.

The fastest fully resolved point found is near phi0 0.10, phi1 0.85, tG 6, T 55, and the limiting pair is always the first one. Dropping temperature one step should add resolution margin for that pair while keeping the same aggressive gradient window, useful for confirming the robust optimum region.

At 55 C, phi1 0.90 was just below the resolution threshold, and dropping to 50 C significantly improved the critical first pair at phi1 0.85. Testing phi1 0.90 at 50 C is the best chance to convert that near-miss into a still faster fully resolved method.

Now that phi1 0.90 works at 50 C with good margin, raise phi0 one step to see if the front can be accelerated further while staying above the resolution threshold. This is the most likely remaining route to an even shorter fully resolved 6 min method.

The final remaining boundary test is to raise phi0 one more step from the fully resolved 0.15/0.90/6/50 method, since that should be the most direct way to shorten the front end further. If it stays above 1.5 for the first pair, it will likely be the fastest fully resolved condition found.
